newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ private sector earnings below forecasts.
newsitem.headline: NZ private sector earnings below forecasts.

text.p: Private sector earnings in the August year released by Statistics New Zealand on Tuesday were below economists's forecasts.

SNZ said total ordinary time earnings for the year to August rose 3.4 percent. Private sector earnings rose 3.7 percent. Economists had forecast a total rise of 3.5 percent but a 4.2 percent rise in the more important private sector.
Public sector earnings rose 3.1 percent in the year.
Statistics New Zealand said average weekly paid hours were lower than they were a week ago.
The average total hourly earnings of employees in August were NZ$16.18, 3.2 percent higher than a year ago. That was slightly down on the 3.3 percent rise in the May year.

The average number of weekly paid hours of employees continued to fall on an annual basis. Full-time equivalent employees were paid for an average of 38.8 hours a week in August, the lowest level since August 1993, and 0.4 percent down from August 1995.
The decrease was due to a 10.1 percent drop in overtime hours between August 1995 and August 1996. Ordinary time hours were unchanged in the same period.
From a recent high of 2.06 hours in November 1994, average overtime hours have fallen to a low of 1.51 hours.
As a result of increased hourly earnings and a fall in paid hours, average weekly earnings of employees increased by 2.8 percent between August 1995 and August 1996.
On average, full-time equivalent employees were earning $627.95 per week in August 1996.
The number of filled jobs in surveyed industries was 1.51 million, up 3.3 percent in the year. There are now 253,100 or 20.2 percent more filled jobs than in 1991.
Slightly more than half of the increase in filled jobs was in jobs filled by women.
There were 1,076,100 full-time jobs, up 3.3 percent in the year but still 2.5 percent down on February 1987.
The largest increase came in the community, social and personal services sector.
Part-time jobs increased by 14,100 or 3.4 percent.
